explication: OpenSSL is a cryptographic toolkit: applications use its command-line tool or libraries to perform cryptographic, certificate, and secure-transport tasks. The main runtime path is user → command dispatcher → selected command → libssl or libcrypto → output or network peer. The README documents TLS, DTLS, QUIC, standalone cryptography, and FIPS capabilities; the tree also shows certificate, CMS, CMP, and OCSP command and library areas. The excerpts clarify QUIC engine ownership of ports and reactor processing, but do not expose most library internals, so those links are intentionally high-level.
